items.q: Axial versus eccentric proptosis localises lesions how?
o: Axial suggests intraconal mass; eccentric displacement points extraconal toward opposite side
items.exp: Muscle cone geometry pushes straight forward when filled from inside and deviates the globe away from outside masses; imaging then hunts glioma or haemangioma versus lacrimal, sinus or metastatic lesions.
r: Incorrect. Thyroid enlarges muscles, often asymmetric.
items.kp: Straight out means inside cone; pushed aside means outside.

items.q: Thyroid eye muscle enlargement spares which structure, distinguishing it from myositis?
items.exp: Graves swells bellies leaving tendons thin on imaging, while idiopathic orbital myositis inflames tendon to sclera with severe pain. This tendon rule guides steroids versus thyroid pathways.
r: Incorrect. Nerve compresses at apex late.
items.kp: Fat bellies, skinny tendons: thyroid eye.

items.q: Active versus burnt out thyroid eye disease management differs how?
o: Active inflammation gets immunotherapy (steroids); fibrotic quiet disease gets rehabilitative surgery
items.exp: Clinical activity scores separate immunosuppression responsive congestion from stable fibrosis needing staged decompression, strabismus and lid repair; operating on hot disease recurs.
r: Incorrect. Hot orbits scar worse operated.
Correct. Cool inflammation first, cut when quiet.
items.kp: Hot eye gets steroids; cold eye gets surgery.

items.q: Child with ethmoid sinusitis, fever, proptosis and painful restricted movements needs what?
o: Urgent contrast CT with IV antibiotics for orbital cellulitis
items.exp: Post septal infection threatens vision and brain through lamina and venous spread; imaging grades abscess needing drainage while antibiotics cover sinus flora. Preseptal disease spares globe function.
r: Incorrect. Allergy lacks fever and ophthalmoplegia.
Correct. Scan and IV treat orbital cellulitis.
items.kp: Fever plus frozen proptosed eye: scan and drip.

items.q: Bilateral chemosis, ophthalmoplegia and sepsis after sinusitis indicate which emergency?
items.exp: Intercavernous connections bilateralise ophthalmic venous congestion with cranial nerve palsies and trigeminal pain; MRI venography confirms and ICU level anticoagulation and antibiotics follow.
r: Incorrect. Dry eye lacks swelling and sepsis.
Incorrect. Episcleritis is sectoral and benign.
items.kp: Both eyes swollen shut with sepsis: cavernous clot.

items.q: Pulsatile proptosis with bruit and corkscrew conjunctival vessels after head trauma suggests what?
items.exp: Internal carotid tear into cavernous sinus arterialises ophthalmic veins, engorging eyes with audible bruit and raised episcleral pressure causing secondary glaucoma; angiography with embolisation treats.
r: Incorrect. Thyroid lacks bruit and pulsation.
Incorrect. Cellulitis is febrile and painful.
items.kp: Whooshing pulsing eye after trauma: fistula.

items.q: Rapidly progressive superonasal orbital mass in a 6 year old most concerning for what?
o: Rhabdomyosarcoma needing urgent biopsy and chemoradiation
items.exp: Paediatric embryonal sarcoma balloons within days with ptosis and displacement; delay metastasises, while prompt tissue with multimodal therapy saves life and often the eye.
r: Incorrect. Dermoids grow slowly since birth.
Incorrect. Chalazion is tarsal and small.
items.kp: Child orbit exploding in days: sarcoma until biopsied.

items.q: Optic nerve sheath meningioma imaging hallmark with slowly progressive vision loss is what?
o: Tram track calcification around the nerve
items.exp: Dural calcification rails the nerve on CT with optociliary shunts on fundus; surgery blinds, so observation or fractionated radiotherapy suits most, reserving excision for blind painful eyes.
items.kp: Rails around nerve with fading vision: sheath meningioma.

items.q: Orbital lymphoma is distinguished from idiopathic inflammation and cellulitis chiefly by what?
o: Painless salmon moulding mass without bony destruction in older adult
items.exp: Low grade marginal zone lymphoma moulds to globe and bone painlessly over months; biopsy with immunophenotyping directs radiation with excellent control. Pain and fever favour inflammation or infection.
items.kp: Quiet pink orbital mass in elderly: lymphoma.

items.q: Compressive optic neuropathy in thyroid eye disease occurs at which site and needs what?
o: Orbital apex crowding; urgent steroids or decompression for dyschromatopsia and field loss
items.exp: Apical muscle crowding strangles nerve function (colour desaturation, afferent pupil defect, field constriction) despite a white quiet eye; vision rescue cannot await rehabilitative staging.
items.kp: Quiet staring eye losing colour vision: apex squeeze.
